import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
data.columns = ['brand', 'model_year', 'megapixels', 'max_iso', 'weight_grams', 'price_usd', 'sensor_type', 'has_video_4k', 'lens_mount', 'body_type']

# Create a bar plot to show the distribution of camera prices
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Camera Prices by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(data['megapixels'], bins=20)
plt.title('Distribution of Megapixels')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('megapixels_histogram.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between weight and price
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='weight_grams', y='price_usd', hue='sensor_type', data=data)
plt.title('Relationship between Weight and Price')
plt.xlabel('Weight (grams)')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('weight_price_scatter.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a pie chart to show the distribution of body types
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.set_palette('viridis')
plt.pie(data['body_type'].value_counts(), labels=data['body_type'].value_counts().index, autopct='%1.1f%%')
plt.title('Distribution of Body Types')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('body_type_pie.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
